name: 243. Chat Completions tool_calls cache_control reaches the Anthropic tool_use block (tool-call-cache-control)
description: Anthropic prompt caching places breakpoints on individual blocks. On /v1/chat/completions a tool call is a tool_calls entry on the assistant message, which Bifrost rewrites into an Anthropic tool_use content block. Before the fix the chat tool-call type had no cache_control field, so a marker placed there was dropped at parse time and never reached Anthropic (the Responses function_call item already carried it). Every case echoes the outgoing provider body via x-bf-send-back-raw-request and pins that the marked tool_use carries cache_control while the unmarked sibling does not. Covers the unified route, the /openai drop-in, Bedrock Mantle (which reuses the Anthropic chat converter for Claude), and Bedrock Converse, where the marker becomes a standalone cachePoint block directly after the toolUse (the same shape the Responses route already emitted). The OpenRouter case pins the four-marker clamp: OpenRouter relays Chat markers to Claude unchanged, so once tool_calls markers were carried a five-marker body started failing with Claude's "maximum of 4 blocks with cache_control" error; the converter now drops the earliest marker in render order, for Claude upstreams only (other OpenRouter upstreams ignore the markers and are left untouched), as the direct Anthropic and Bedrock paths already did. The OpenAI-target case pins the strip: the marker is a Bifrost extension on the OpenAI-shaped ingress, so for OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible targets the egress removes it from tool_calls exactly as it already did for content blocks and tool definitions, while OpenRouter keeps all of them.

exec: pm.test('anthropic unified: multi-turn tool conversation with cache_control on a tool_calls entry succeeds', function () {
pm.test('anthropic unified: cache_control on the tool_calls entry reaches the Anthropic tool_use block (was silently dropped before the fix)', function () {
pm.expect(toolUses.length, 'expected 2 tool_use blocks, raw assistant=' + JSON.stringify(assistant)).to.equal(2);
pm.expect(toolUses[0].cache_control, 'first tool_use lost its cache_control: ' + JSON.stringify(toolUses[0])).to.eql({ type: 'ephemeral' });
pm.expect(toolUses[1].cache_control, 'second tool_use must not gain a marker it was never given').to.equal(undefined);
